business_problem: Shandong Port Group needed to improve logistics transparency, customer service, and multimodal coordination because information was fragmented across port systems, service standards differed between locations, and customers increasingly expected personalized, real-time support across shipping, customs, routing, and cargo tracking.
solution_summary: Shandong Port Group is piloting a large-model-based external supply-chain service platform with Baidu AI Cloud. The core stack uses the Qianfan Large Model Platform and BaiGe Heterogeneous Compute Platform to power six agent-style applications: Shipowner Butler, Smart Route Navigator, Port Encyclopedia, Smart Tracking, Smart Customs Clearance, and Smart Price Inquiry. Rather than treating the model as a generic chatbot, the project applies language understanding, generation, reasoning, natural-language processing, and BI analysis to specific customer-facing port workflows. Each agent is aligned to a user group such as shipowners, shipping agents, truck drivers, cargo owners, freight forwarders, or customs-facing operations, and exposes functions such as vessel-status queries, policy Q&A, code matching, route and cost planning, or real-time cargo tracking.

solution_components.name: Qianfan Large Model Platform
solution_components.role: Provides the large-model application layer that powers the six supply-chain service agents.

solution_components.name: BaiGe Heterogeneous Compute Platform
solution_components.role: Supplies the compute foundation needed to run large-model inference and related AI services for the port group.

data_flow: Port, customs, maritime, vessel, cargo, and route information is fed into six role-specific AI agents. The model layer interprets requests, generates answers and recommendations, and returns guidance such as vessel status, business-process explanations, cargo tracking, customs help, and transport price planning to different users in the logistics chain.
business_outcome: Shandong Port gained a unified AI service hub that can reduce port dwell time, improve service quality for many logistics stakeholders, and accelerate the transformation toward a smarter, more efficient port supply chain.
architecture_clues: The project positions the model layer as a unified 'port AI hub' for external supply-chain services
Different agents are mapped to distinct external user groups rather than one generic interface
The source emphasizes BI analysis alongside language understanding, reasoning, and NLP capabilities
evidence_quotes: The project uses large-model technology to build six intelligent-agent applications for Shandong Port's supply-chain services (original: 以大模型技术构建六大智能体应用，赋能山东港口供应链服务).

Shandong Port wanted AI and big data to address information asymmetry, weak data sharing, poor multimodal coordination, and inconsistent service standards (original: 物流信息不对称…缺乏统一的信息平台…多式联运发展缓慢…服务流程不一致).

The solution includes Shipowner Butler, Smart Route Navigator, Port Encyclopedia, Smart Tracking, Smart Customs Clearance, and Smart Price Inquiry (original: 本次建设内容主要包括：船东管家、智途领航、口岸宝典、智能跟踪、智能通关以及智行问价六个智能体应用).

The expected outcome is lower dwell time for vehicles, vessels, and cargo and better logistics efficiency for cargo owners, freight forwarders, shipowners, customs, and drivers (original: 这将有助于降低“车船货”在港停时，减少物流成本，提升社会综合物流效率).
